subject: Urgent: East Coast CS - targeted retention & manager action plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: East Coast CS - engagement drop flagged (summary + ask)

Team —

Quick heads-up from the engagement digest: the East Coast CS pod (12 people) shows a 21% drop in manager-scored engagement vs. Q1, with two voluntary attrition signals (passive job board activity + flagged 1:1 notes). I attached the survey excerpt that highlights lower scores for "clear career pathway" and "recognition."

This feels time-sensitive because one of the account owners (Acme Health) is at risk of churn if we lose coverage. I propose:
- Managers do focused 1:1s this week using the attached checklist.
- Leadership calibrates a small retention package (one-time bonus / role clarification) for at-risk contributors by EOD Friday.
- PeopleOps confirms program guardrails and approval path.

Can Laura/Marissa run manager outreach and capture which individuals are high-priority? PeopleOps, please confirm approval timeline.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of CS Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: engagement_survey_excerpt.pdf, mgr_action_checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: East Coast CS - engagement drop flagged (summary + ask)

Thanks Hannah — will take point. Quick update on ops plan:

1) Manager outreach: Marissa and I will split 1:1s (6 each). Planned questions are in the checklist; we'll add an explicit ask about current offers/counter-offers and career interest.
2) Capture: we'll use the shared sheet in Drive (link below) to log: name, tenure, risk signals, manager notes, suggested retention action.
3) Draft retention language: I put together a one-page template (will circulate) we can use for approvals.

Timing: Managers will finish 1:1s by Thu EOD (21 May). We'll handoff high-priority list to PeopleOps on Fri morning for approvals.

Two asks for leadership:
- Can Vivek confirm if a discretionary one-time credit up to $7.5k per person is within scope for quick approvals?
- If we proceed with offers, who signs communications? (Vivek vs. PeopleOps)

Onward —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success Ops

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: East Coast CS - engagement drop flagged (summary + ask)

Appreciate the fast triage. I support a targeted retention package for high-risk contributors tied to clear manager commitments (career plan + 90-day milestones). Parameters:
- Approval ceiling: $7.5k one-time discretionary (per person) — must be justified by manager note and business impact.
- Max headcount: initial approval for up to 3 individuals in this pod, further approvals require PeopleOps + Finance.
- Communication: offers should come from PeopleOps HR with leadership looped.

Let's do a short calibration call Friday 12:00 - 12:30 ET to confirm the three names and draft language. Laura, please share the prioritized list before noon.

Thanks —
Vivek
VP, Customer & Revenue Operations

- Manager justification (one paragraph)
- Candidate impact statement (why retention vs. backfill)
- Signed manager development plan attached to the offer

We will prepare the offer packet and send from hr@redwoodinference.com once we receive the materials. Timeline: if we receive required docs by Fri 1300 ET, we can issue offers same day; any delay pushes to Monday.

Also copying our external counsel (Ankit) for any phrasing that could be construed as contractual.

All —

Recap and mutual action plan after the calibration call:

1) Managers complete 1:1s (Laura/Marissa) — deliverable: prioritized list with manager paragraph + development plan attached (Drive link). Due: Fri 22 May 12:00 ET.
2) PeopleOps prepares offer packet using retention_offer_template.docx and issues from hr@redwoodinference.com once docs received. Target issue: Fri 22 May 17:00 ET (contingent).
3) Leadership to approve up to 3 discretionary credits at $7.5k ceiling. Vivek will sign off final list.
4) If any candidate responds with counter-offer or escalates externally, loop in Legal and Sales leader owning the account (Megan from Acme — cc'd in this thread) for continuity planning.
